story_type: fishermen abandon a drifting, powerless boat into cold open sea, helicopter hoists all three from the water
hook: Three fishermen went into the sea, 58 miles off Alaska.
narration: Three fishermen abandoned ship in fifteen foot seas, fifty eight miles off Alaska.
An electrical fire had killed their boat's power. Even at anchor, the Tsiu kept drifting, at risk of running aground.
The first call came at four twenty three a.m. A Jayhawk crew from Air Station Sitka arrived at seven minutes past noon.
The wind was twenty nine miles an hour. The air and the water were both forty seven degrees.
Water pulls heat from a body far faster than air does, so the rescue swimmer rode the cable straight down to them.
One by one, the crew hoisted all three survivors out of the sea.
outcome: All three were flown to Yakutat, where they were reported in stable condition.
title: Abandoned ship 58 miles off Alaska
description:
An Air Station Sitka MH-60 Jayhawk crew hoists three fishermen from the water after they abandoned the drifting fishing vessel Tsiu 58 miles east of Kayak Island, Alaska, on Nov. 10, 2024.

extra_sources.excerpt: ANCHORAGE, Alaska — The Coast Guard rescued three survivors after they abandoned ship 58 miles east of Kayak Island, Alaska, Sunday.

An MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter crew from Coast Guard Air Station Sitka recovered all three survivors from the water and safely transported them to Yakutat where they were reported to be in stable condition.

Watchstanders at Coast Guard Sector Western Alaska and U.S. Arctic command center received notification at 4:23 a.m. from fishing vessel Tsiu after they lost power due to an electrical fire. The vessel deployed its anchor but continued drifting and was at risk of running aground.
The helicopter crew arrived on scene at 12:07 p.m. and hoisted all three survivors from the water.
On-scene weather at the time was 29-mph winds, 15-foot seas with an air and water temperature of 47 degrees.
